text:
marta_customer: Hey team — our March invoice shows 720 reserved GPU hours for pool `dedicated-prod-42`, but the Dedicated dashboard (per-route view) only reports ~480 reserved hours used. Also, SLA credit that was promised after the outage on Mar 14 didn't appear on the invoice. Can someone help reconcile?

oliver_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Marta. We'll triage. Quick questions: is `dedicated-prod-42` the only pool affected? Do you have the account/org id and the invoice number?

marta_customer: Yep just that pool. Org: ACME-Corp, invoice: INV-2024-03-ACME. I can paste the minimal repro we used to generate load — we ran steady 12 concurrent streams for 6 hours starting 2024-03-14T03:00Z. Example API call: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer {{KEY}}" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-dedicated-v1","pool_id":"dedicated-prod-42","prompt":"..."}'`

raj_patil: Thanks. I pulled metering logs for pool `dedicated-prod-42` between 2024-03-14T03:00Z and 2024-03-14T09:30Z. Token burn looks consistent with your runs, but I see multiple `host_id` values in the request notes: some requests were executed on hosts labeled `burst-host-*` which are not attached to the reserved billing meter. That can cause reserved-hours to undercount while invoice shows committed hours.

lina_prod_metrics: Adding context — our dashboard aggregates by `billing_cluster` tag. If a host serves via burst routing without the `billing_cluster=dedicated-prod-42` tag, the usage falls back to on-demand metering. Invoice generation uses commit records and reserved capacity assignments, so we can end up double-counting: invoice deducts reserved commit even if runtime was billed as on-demand due to tag mismatch.

marta_customer: Ugh. We definitely saw routing to burst when autoscaler spun up. Is that something we can prevent? We rely on reserved capacity for predictable costs.

raj_patil: Two immediate repro steps to check on your end: 1) in your requests include `X-Redwood-Pool: dedicated-prod-42` header (we saw some clients omit it and rely on the SDK default). 2) confirm your pool's instance labels: `billing_cluster=dedicated-prod-42`. Internally we ran: `SELECT ts, host_id, pool_id, billing_cluster FROM metering.events WHERE pool_id='dedicated-prod-42' AND ts BETWEEN '2024-03-14T03:00Z' AND '2024-03-14T09:30Z'` — you can share results if you'd like.

sre_oncall: FWIW I checked autoscaler activity at that window. There was a scaling event at 03:11Z that created instances with missing metadata (bug in our bootstrap script), those hosts were assigned to burst routing temporarily. I've opened PR to fix bootstrap tagging, but that doesn't retroactively fix billing for that window.

billing-bot: Automated update: Invoice INV-2024-03-ACME has an open billing review (case# BIL-2489). SLA credit calculation deferred pending reconciliation of reserved vs on-demand attributions.

oliver_support: We're escalating to Billing Ops to reconcile commit records vs metering. Action items: (1) Billing ops to compute net delta for INV-2024-03-ACME and apply SLA credit if appropriate, (2) SRE to backfill missing host metadata for 2024-03-14 window so metering attribution can be corrected, (3) Customer to add `X-Redwood-Pool` header or confirm SDK config to prevent client-side misrouting. I'll file internal ticket INT-2024-443 and copy you, Marta.

marta_customer: Thanks — appreciate the quick triage. Please keep me posted on the SLA credit outcome.

oliver_support: Will do. Marking as escalated to Billing Ops / SRE. :thumbsup:
